item.title: the fetus
item.description:
The fetus unfurls its body from the small black stone it folded itself around.

It stretches, reaching its arms back, back back, fingers branching into my shoulders, my neck, my skull.

Its legs go down, down down, toes curling into my stomach, my legs, my thighs, sinking into my ankles.

I feel my body turn leaden. My blood vitrified.

A gray cast covers my eyes and the world around me drifts away.

item.title: [DRAFT] Journal Entry from August 2, 2026: I get to hear 'no'
item.description:
Sunday

9:42 PM

For a long time, women’s romantic lives were shaped more by circumstance than by choice.

Well, that’s not entirely true. Choice was a factor, but everyone except for the woman in question had the right to decide. Economics decided. Politics decided. Families decided. Marriage was less about affection, compatibility, or love, and more about survival.

But my life is different. I get to choose who I love. I get to tell someone that I think they’re beautiful. I get to ask the question.

item.title: [DRAFT] I <3 NY
item.description: A man wheeled a bright blue dresser across an intersection while a yellow taxi van squeezed around him. Restaurant workers dragged trash bags into alleyways. An Amazon employee dragged a wheelbarrow full of boxes behind him. A father checked his GPS again and again before turning to wave his family in the right direction. Everyone looked tiny, like ants against the sprawl of the gray and brick buildings rising all around them.

item.title: the girl
item.description:
maybe we’ll all dance one day bare feet on dewy grass- all of us stepping out from the shadows to show the world our faces.

the light and the dark.

I walk the hallways of my memory and gather all my selves.

I hold the hand of the woman who stayed too long hug the one who left.

but I never know what to say to the girl.

sometimes I find myself standing in front of her door, cracking it open, peering inside.

item.title: kismet
item.description:
to be be pink and then be blue and to burn and to be born again and again.

to be brave and to be broken to be home and to be displaced again and again.

to stand and to fall and to love, to have my soul crushed and my wings ripped out to stand in the mirror and watch my back bleed again and again.

my kismet to live and to die again and again, give my soul to these strangers again and again.

item.title: scream
item.description:
I bow my head to the forest, forgive me in advance.

I’m draped by the trees as the wave rolls through me.

I lift my face up I can’t see the sky.

I can’t contain her anymore.

I open my mouth and scream.

The sound crashes out of me.

Water pours from my eyes Wind escapes from my ears.

Fire ripples all around me trees uprooted mountains split open creatures spill from their recesses making tracks far away from here.

item.title: untitled 00
item.description:
I still pray the way she taught me.

I used to ask God with all my heart to let me fly I used to ask God with all my heart to let me die.

item.title: Excuse Me, Do You Know That Place?
item.description:
Excuse me, do you know that place?

Where the table is set, Forks and knives lined neatly next to clean plates topped with warm meals?

Have you seen it?

Have you felt it?

Sinking into a hug after a long day, a long week, a long time.

Can you take me there?

I can’t count on myself to find it anymore.

Can you take me?

So I can lay my head and rest, free my mind of the burdens I’ve carried, the burdens I’ve made.

item.title: Mama
item.description:
Mama, I want to ask you about you.

But I’m scared of what you’ll say. I’m scared that the stories you’ll tell will make my sadness stay.

I feel tired, Mama. How do I ask you for help?

When today I am the one holding you, telling you it’ll be okay.

item.title: The People Are Dying Here
item.description:
Little boys run through the streets, crumpled bills in their pockets, selling fruit under the sky, weaving through traffic in the hot sun.

Little girls push their legs closed, and keep their mouths shut, sneak their eyes open during prayer, fingertips burnt from flipping tortillas.

They watch someone’s dreams play out on a neighbor’s TV.

They’re hungry for more.

The children are dying there, the children are crying there.

Angela only saw her mother on the weekend before the sickness took over.

item.title: behind the walls
item.description:
little woman, big girl.

the garden i grow is a home you’ll never see; a world you’ll never know.

I worked tirelessly, living only off of the hope that you would see it and smile.

I dream of it the day our hands touch again. I’ll show you all the fruit I grew out of my tears and you’ll pick me up and we’ll run across the world leaving my garden to rot.

item.title: you'll cry
item.description:
You’ll cry about it. You’ll cry until your eyes dry out, hot tears like the sidewalk in the summer on the day you crumpled to the ground, trying to remember where you were going and what you were saying and who you were loving and when did you lose them.

You’ll cry until your eyes are too swollen to stay open and your nose is as red as the sun pressing against your eyelids as you lay in the field by the lake where you leaned in to kiss the person who disappeared as quickly as they had arrived, leaving only the ghost of their fingers in your hair for memory.
